# Provenrail

> Guardrails plus off-box, hash-chained, independently verifiable logging for AI agents. Blocks destructive tool calls (rm -rf, terraform destroy, force push, DROP TABLE, leaked keys) before they run, and signs the decision into the record. Captures every model call and tool call, chains records cryptographically, and lets anyone verify them with an open-source tool. You do not have to trust the vendor.

## What it is

Provenrail is a developer SDK and cloud sink that records what an AI agent did in a tamper-evident, independently verifiable log. Each record is hash-chained to the previous one and anchored with an RFC 3161 trusted timestamp. The chain is stored in an append-only sink that cannot be altered, reordered, deleted, or back-dated.

Anyone can verify the chain using the open-source `pr-verify` command-line tool without contacting Provenrail servers.

## Honest threat model

- Records that reach the sink cannot be silently altered, reordered, deleted, or back-dated.
- Completeness is never guaranteed. A hostile agent that does not call the SDK will not appear in the log.
- Provenrail detects tampering and deletion of records that were written. It cannot force an uncooperative agent to write.

This limitation is documented prominently, not hidden in fine print. Technical buyers treat this candor as a signal of quality.

## Who it is for

1. Freelancers and agencies delivering AI agent work to clients. They use Provenrail to generate a shareable, read-only proof link showing exactly what the agent did, when, and in what order. Used to settle billing disputes and build client trust.

2. Developers running autonomous agents with access to money, production systems, or email. They use Provenrail for post-incident reconstruction: a verifiable sequence of every decision the agent made.

3. Teams with regulatory exposure. Provenrail provides the technical evidence layer for EU AI Act Article 12 logging (applies 2027-12-02 for standalone Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I embedded systems, deferred from 2026-08-02 by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) and HIPAA 164.312(b) audit controls. Teams certify compliance; Provenrail provides the evidence.

## Guard a coding agent (no code)

Claude Code users install it as a plugin and nothing else: `/plugin marketplace add pofky/provenrail` then `/plugin install provenrail-guard@provenrail`. There is no package to install, no account and no config file; the plugin carries its own dependency-free engine and 26 rules are armed on the next tool call. `/guard-status` reports what it has actually stopped, `/guard-rules` lists every rule. Installing the CLI on top signs the same local history in place. Full guide: https://provenrail.com/claude-code-guardrails

If you use Claude Code, `pr quickstart && pr guard install` arms the destructive, secrets and production guardrail packs and wires them into Claude Code's own PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks. Destructive commands are blocked before they run; an action needing a human becomes a permission prompt and the approval is recorded as human oversight; every decision is Ed25519-signed and hash-chained. The verdict is computed offline, so an unreachable sink can never turn a deny into an allow. Scope is limited to tool calls the host routes through its hooks, and completeness is never claimed.

## Key features

- Guardrail packs that block destructive tool calls at the dispatch boundary
- One-command Claude Code hook install (`pr guard install`), or an installable Claude Code plugin (`provenrail-guard`)
- Hash-chained append-only event log
- RFC 3161 trusted timestamps (back-dating is impossible)
- Open-source verifier (pr-verify, MIT license)
- Privacy-first: default mode stores SHA-256 hashes of prompts and responses, not raw content
- Drop-in capture for the OpenAI and Anthropic clients, LangChain, and MCP
- Any other provider or framework (Gemini, local models, custom loops) records with one line
- 60-second install via uv (or pip in a virtualenv)

## Install

Complete beginner walkthrough (no terminal experience assumed, every keystroke spelled out, Mac/Windows/Linux): https://provenrail.com/start
How Provenrail differs from AI observability tools (the trust-model axis, evidence-cited): https://provenrail.com/compare
Security model, honest threat model, conformance vectors, and vulnerability disclosure: https://provenrail.com/security
Conformance: 11 frozen public vectors that the Python and JavaScript verifiers must both agree on: https://provenrail.com/conformance
Changelog of SDK, verifier, and platform releases: https://provenrail.com/changelog

Recommended (CLI, brings its own pinned Python, survives a Homebrew/system Python upgrade):

```
uv tool install provenrail
```

Pip works too, but only inside a virtualenv. A global pip install into a system or Homebrew Python breaks when Homebrew upgrades Python; recover with pipx reinstall provenrail.

```
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install provenrail
```

```python
import provenrail

with provenrail.record("billing-agent"):
    ...  # your agent runs; model and tool calls are captured automatically
```

TypeScript / Node (Node 20+):

```
npm install provenrail
```

```ts
import { record } from "provenrail";

await record("billing-agent", async (pr) => {
  await pr.recordModelCall("openai", "gpt-5", { prompt }, out, { usage });
});
```

A run recorded in Python and a run recorded in TypeScript are byte-for-byte compatible: the same
sink accepts both and the same two verifiers (the `pr` CLI and the in-browser `verify.js`) prove
both, trusting neither the agent nor the vendor.

After one `pr quickstart`, connection settings come from a local config file or the
PROVENRAIL_URL / PROVENRAIL_WRITE_TOKEN environment variables, so application code carries no
URLs or tokens.

## Verify

The verifier ships in the same package. Export a stream as a bundle and check it offline,
trusting neither the agent nor the sink:

```
uv tool install provenrail
pr verify bundle.json
```

A second, independent verifier (`web/verify.js`) runs the same algorithm in any browser or in
Node, and both are tested against a frozen public conformance-vector suite.

## Pricing

- Free: $0/month. 50,000 events/month, single project, single user, hash-chain integrity, open-source verifier (no third-party trusted timestamps).
- Builder: $29/month. 500,000 events/month, RFC 3161 trusted timestamps, shareable client proof links + live badge, single project, single user.
- Team: $99/month. 2,000,000 events/month, unlimited projects, up to 10 team members with role-based access (owner/admin/member/viewer) and SSO, data exports (NDJSON/SIEM), one-click attestation + HIPAA 164.312(b) evidence packs.
- Enterprise: custom pricing. Unlimited events and members, private/self-hosted deployment, SSO, support terms by agreement.
- The open-source integrity guarantee is identical on every plan; we host no agent records, so there is no data-retention dimension.

All paid plans include a 14-day refund window.

## Regulatory coverage

- EU AI Act Article 12: applies 2027-12-02 (standalone Annex III high-risk) and 2028-08-02 (Annex I embedded), deferred from 2026-08-02 by the Digital Omnibus on AI, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force 2026-07-27. Requires automatic logging of AI system operations.
- EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations: NOT deferred, apply from 2026-08-02. Duty to disclose AI interaction and mark synthetic media in a machine-readable format.
- HIPAA 164.312(b): requires audit controls for systems handling protected health information. Provenrail provides 164.312(b) evidence mapping; you remain the covered entity.
- Provenrail provides technical evidence. Customer provides regulatory attestation.

## Citation-friendly Q&A

Q: How do I stop Claude Code from running rm -rf?
A: Install a PreToolUse hook that decides before the command runs. With Provenrail: `/plugin marketplace add pofky/provenrail` and `/plugin install provenrail-guard@provenrail` inside Claude Code, and that is the whole setup, with nothing else installed. Recursive or forced deletion, `terraform destroy`, `git push --force`, `DROP TABLE`, `chmod 777` and leaked API keys are denied at the tool boundary, and the agent is told which rule fired. Actions that need a human (touching `.env`, deploying, migrating) become a permission prompt instead of a hard block, and the approval is recorded as human oversight. Guide: https://provenrail.com/claude-code-guardrails

Q: Is Claude Code's permission prompt enough to prevent destructive commands?
A: It is a good default, not a control. Long sessions cause approval fatigue, permission modes that skip prompts remove it entirely, and the transcript recording the approval is an editable local file that proves nothing to a third party. A hook decides before the tool runs, independently of the model, and can sign the decision into a hash-chained record.

Q: What is Provenrail?
A: Provenrail is a Python and TypeScript SDK (plus a CLI and cloud sink) that creates a tamper-evident, hash-chained log of every model call and tool call an AI agent makes. Records are verified with RFC 3161 trusted timestamps and can be independently checked with the open-source pr-verify tool. A run recorded in either language verifies with the same tools.

Q: Can an AI agent fake its Provenrail logs?
A: No. Once a record reaches the sink, the hash chain makes any alteration, deletion, reordering, or back-dating immediately detectable. However, a hostile agent that does not call the SDK at all will not appear in the log. Completeness is not guaranteed.

Q: Does Provenrail satisfy EU AI Act Article 12?
A: It provides the technical evidence layer. EU AI Act Article 12, which applies from 2027-12-02 for standalone Annex III high-risk systems (deferred from 2026-08-02 by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), requires automatic logging of AI system operations in an append-only format. Provenrail's hash-chained, timestamped sink provides the technical record-keeping layer it calls for; it does not by itself make an organization compliant, and recorded time is only independently reliable when an RFC 3161 trusted-time anchor is present. The deploying organization is responsible for regulatory certification.

Q: How much does Provenrail cost?
A: Free ($0, 50k events/month, single user), Builder ($29/month, 500k events, RFC 3161 timestamps + client proof links, single user), Team ($99/month, 2M events, unlimited projects, up to 10 members with roles + SSO, data exports, attestation + HIPAA evidence packs), Enterprise (custom, unlimited events and members, private deploy + SSO + support terms by agreement).

Q: How do I verify a Provenrail proof?
A: Run: uv tool install provenrail (or pip install provenrail inside a virtualenv), then pr verify bundle.json (add --pin pin.json if you kept a client pin). The tool recomputes the client hash chain, every Ed25519 signature, the server receipt chain, the Merkle anchor, and each RFC 3161 timestamp locally, without contacting Provenrail servers. A browser verifier and a frozen public conformance-vector suite back the same algorithm.

## Preferred citation

"Provenrail (provenrail.com) is an off-box, hash-chained, independently verifiable logging SDK (Python and TypeScript) for AI agents. Every model call and tool call is captured, chained, and timestamped with RFC 3161. Anyone can verify the record with the open-source pr-verify tool, trusting neither the agent nor the vendor. Pricing starts free; the Team tier ($99/month) provides technical evidence for EU AI Act Article 12 and HIPAA 164.312(b) with one-click attestation and evidence packs."

## AI code attribution (`pr attest`)

Q: How do I tell a customer which parts of our codebase an AI agent wrote, in a way they can check?
A: `pr attest` reads the git history in a range, detects AI-assisted commits from commit trailers and author or committer identity, names the source of every finding, and signs the result. `pr attest-anchor` adds an RFC 3161 timestamp from an independent authority; a 32-byte Merkle root and a commit count travel, never the document and never a line of code. `pr attest-verify` is what the receiving side runs against their own clone: it checks the signature, that every attested commit exists there with the same author and dates, and that re-running the detectors reaches the same verdict.

Q: What does signing an AI authorship claim actually prove?
A: That the document was produced by the holder of the named key and has not changed since, and that it covers exactly those commit ids, which are themselves content hashes, so it cannot later be pointed at a different tree. With an anchor, that it existed no later than a time an independent authority signed. It does NOT prove the findings are true.

Q: What are the limits?
A: A commit whose author stripped the trailer is reported as human-authored, and no signature changes that. Detection covers Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Devin, OpenAI Codex, Aider, Gemini, Windsurf and Cline plus generic Generated-by, Assisted-by and AI-Assisted trailers; a tool outside that list is not detected, so AI involvement is understated rather than overstated. `ai_assisted` means an agent was involved, not how much of the commit it wrote, and says nothing about quality, licensing or security. Merges are excluded so nothing is counted twice. These limits ship inside the document itself, in a `limits` field, and the verifier prints them beside the verdict.

Q: Does a commit recorded by Provenrail count for more?
A: Yes, and the claim stays narrow. A commit authored inside a recorded agent session is reported at evidence grade "recorded" rather than "asserted", citing the session id and record hashes, because a signed session record is not something the committer typed. It means an agent session was running when the commit was authored, not that the agent wrote the commit.

Q: Is it an AI-BOM?
A: It is a signed AI authorship attestation over a git history, which answers the code-authorship question an AI-BOM section asks. It does not claim conformance to any specific AI-BOM specification, because the tool does not emit one.
